objective: Attribute and reduce pod-creation-to-first-token restore latency while preserving correctness, memory, security, and the immutable V1 baseline.

kv_cache_release.mechanism: vLLM sleep level 1 after a fail-closed drain, followed by wake-up after restore
kv_cache_release.rationale: The retained source checkpoint was created before customer traffic, so its preallocated KV cache has no request state worth preserving. vLLM 0.27.1 level-1 sleep clears caches, offloads weights to CPU, and discards the KV allocation while retaining enough state to wake after restore.
preconditions: empty logical KV and prefix caches
vLLM sleep mode and cuMem allocator supported by the pinned runtime
checkpoint source remains drained until checkpoint completion
prepare_sequence: remove readiness and stop new request admission
drain and prove zero in-flight requests
clear logical prefix and encoder caches
invoke vLLM sleep level 1 in wait mode
verify sleeping state and minimum GPU-memory release
create the checkpoint only after every assertion passes
restore_sequence: restore CRIU and CUDA while the engine remains non-ready
verify the expected GPU-memory envelope and an empty logical cache
publish readiness only after every restore invariant passes
failure_behavior: checkpoint aborts if drain cannot be proven
checkpoint aborts if GPU memory release is below the acceptance floor
restore remains non-ready if wake-up or cache reallocation fails
no partial candidate checkpoint may replace or alias the retained V1 checkpoint
restore_invariants: readiness remains false until KV cache reallocation and a valid inference probe complete
logical KV and prefix caches are empty after restore
model revision weights and output-validity contract match V1
post-wake GPU memory remains within five percent of V1

control_plane.required_boundary: authenticated Pod-local or Unix-socket control path that is absent from every Service and Ingress

required_tests: checkpoint is rejected with any in-flight request
checkpoint is rejected when sleep or memory-release verification fails
sleep and wake are idempotent or fail explicitly on duplicate control messages
restore never becomes ready before wake-up completes
two valid post-restore responses with an empty logical KV cache
control endpoint is unreachable outside the Pod
candidate checkpoint is at most sixty percent of V1 size
V0 I1 and V1 artifacts remain byte-for-byte unchanged

optimization_backlog.name: right-sized elastic KV cache
optimization_backlog.idea: Replace gpu-memory-utilization=0.85 with a capacity-derived initial KV allocation and expand only after readiness when demand requires it.
optimization_backlog.risk: Changes concurrency and throughput capacity; requires a separate pressure campaign.

optimization_backlog.name: CUDA-graph diet
optimization_backlog.idea: Retain only graph capture sizes supported by observed request shapes, or rebuild low-priority graphs after the first-token readiness gate.
optimization_backlog.risk: Graph recapture can move saved checkpoint time into post-restore latency.

optimization_backlog.name: weight externalization
optimization_backlog.idea: Keep immutable weights outside CRIU and reconnect them through GMS, ModelExpress, or a supported local-NVMe/GDS path while CRIU restores only process state.
optimization_backlog.risk: Architectural change; GMS plus Snapshot remains ineligible under the pinned Dynamo release.

optimization_backlog.name: frontend-engine split checkpoint
optimization_backlog.idea: Checkpoint only EngineCore and launch the lightweight API frontend concurrently during restore.
optimization_backlog.risk: Introduces a new process boundary and reconnection protocol for a modest size reduction.

optimization_backlog.name: semantic allocation manifest
optimization_backlog.idea: Tag allocations as preserve, recreate-before-ready, or recreate-in-background so the snapshot stores only correctness-critical pages.
optimization_backlog.risk: Requires vLLM and CUDA allocator integration plus strict address-stability tests.

optimization_backlog.name: parallel restore with a node-local hot tier
optimization_backlog.idea: Combine the reduced checkpoint with bounded asynchronous CRIU reads and a digest-verified RAM or NVMe node cache.
optimization_backlog.risk: Reduces transfer time rather than bytes and needs memory-pressure and cache-coherency controls.

stages.name: V2-A-instrumented-supported-path
stages.purpose: Reproduce the supported non-GMS path with complete phase and storage telemetry and test whether the V1 tail is storage/cache driven.
allowed_changes: new seed run IDs and artifact directory
forbidden_changes: model command image driver GPU node or checkpoint format changes
V0 I1 or V1 artifact changes

stages.name: V2-B-experimental-optimization
stages.purpose: Evaluate exactly one size or restore-path optimization against V2-A after its bottleneck is confirmed.
constraints: new candidate image digest and compatibility hash
never override a disabled safety feature gate
GMS is ineligible while Dynamo v1.3.0 documents GMS plus Snapshot as disabled

no_go: any restore failure or invalid response
GPU memory deviation above five percent
secret exposure or service-account token mount
median p95 or maximum first-token target missed

security_invariants: empty KV cache at checkpoint source
fail-closed manifest image-history and admitted-pod secret audit
performance_safety: bounded sequential campaign with one active measured workload
capture baseline expected stress and recovery telemetry before optimization claims
abort on node pressure GPU Xid I/O errors or correctness failure
do not infer capacity from page-cache-warm results
rollback: do not modify or delete V0/I1/V1 artifacts
retain namespace PVC checkpoint image and keys until approved cleanup
stop V2 pods and observers without changing retained V1 resources
revert by selecting the immutable V1 candidate image and checkpoint
